claims.reason: Cited text states the goal is to detect and rank humorous statements using a Language Model approach.
Cited text explicitly gives both reasons: learning a style of humor and assigning probabilities enabling relative ranking.
Cited text directly states the system estimated tweet probabilities using Ngram language models built from funny tweets and news corpora, scoring by probability per model.
Cited text states higher probability under the funny model is funnier and lower probability under the news model is funnier since least like the news corpus.
Cited text confirms use of bigrams and trigrams as features and KenLM with modified Kneser-Ney smoothing and back-off.
Cited text states a particular sense of humor is learned from humorous tweets submitted to hashtag prompts from @midnight with Chris Hardwick.
Cited text describes participation in SemEval-2017 Task 6 with Subtask A pairwise comparison and Subtask B semi-ranking into the specified categories.
Cited text states news-trained models had a significant advantage, bigrams slightly better than trigrams, and news trigram models placed fourth in Subtask A and first in Subtask B.
Cited text states the limitation is large out-of-vocabulary words and that increasing training data cannot solve it because humor relies on creative language like puns on invented words.
